name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,610

clue.text: Delay interrupting student's instruction

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a tutee is a student being taught by a tutor
a lag is a delay or time lapse

explanation.surface: A student complains that holdups keep breaking into their lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition: LAG goes inside TUTEE to give TUTELAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is teaching or guidance given by a tutor, a direct synonym of instruction.

clue.text: Hostess perhaps needs someone present below stairs

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written below another simply follows it

blocks.note: a flight is a set of stairs
an attendant is someone who is present, as at a meeting

explanation.surface: A party hostess needs a servant waiting downstairs, below stairs in the old servants' quarters sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below stairs' looks like a single phrase for servants' quarters, but 'below' is a placing instruction and 'stairs' is a flight. 'Perhaps' flags the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Air hostess is the older term for cabin crew, so a hostess is one example of this airline job.

clue.text: What's involved adapting an endangered species?

indicators.note: something involved is tangled and complicated, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A conservationist asks what it takes to help a threatened species adapt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adapting' sounds like the action in question, but here it is just raw letters with 'an' to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a famous example of an animal long listed as vulnerable or at risk of extinction.

clue.text: Selfish endeavour say to put up inscription on tomb

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
taken as written
RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones

explanation.surface: Someone vain wants to put up their own epitaph on a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like erecting the inscription, but it only turns the little word 'to' upside down in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity pursued mainly to boost one's own self-importance, hence a selfish undertaking.

clue.text: Hooligan beheaded with Old English instrument

indicators.note: losing the head means the opening letter is cut off

blocks.note: a yob is a hooligan; without its first letter it leaves two letters
OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: A thug is beheaded with some antique English weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: YOB is British slang for a lout; behead it to get OB.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind, one example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Sensational clanger — poor don had to go into it

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a different order
to go into something is to enter it, so one piece is set inside another

blocks.note: a clanger is British slang for an embarrassing mistake
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecturer makes an astonishing gaffe and has to get stuck into sorting it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' is needed as fodder along with 'don' and 'to'; 'it' points back to the clanger, which receives the shuffled letters after BL. Dropping a clanger is a British idiom for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-and-thunder describes melodramatic, violent, lurid entertainment, so it is a close match for sensational.

clue.text: Wine container church needed to hold a service

indicators.note: holding something means having it enclosed within, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written
the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A church needs a wine vessel to hold a communion service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests worship in this churchy scene, but it is a military service, the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open-topped glass flask used for serving wine at the table.

clue.text: Cow in government primarily engaged in this?

definitions.text: Cow in government primarily engaged in this?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wry question: is intimidation what goes on in government above all?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like an animal but is the verb to intimidate. The whole clue also hints at the answer: what those in government chiefly do, it suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark signals a cryptic reading of the whole clue, implying ministers mainly intimidate others, which is what bullying means.

clue.text: Everyone getting into wicked tune

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: wicked means bad
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole crowd gets into a fantastic tune, with wicked in its slang sense of great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' reads as slang approval of the tune, but it is the plain sense, BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, often slow and narrative, so it is a kind of tune.

clue.text: Dramatic princess entertaining American president

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your home, so one piece houses another

blocks.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A stage-struck royal hosts a visiting US head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American president' looks like one phrase for the definition, but 'American' supplies the A that goes inside Lear's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth president of the United States, serving through most of the 1980s.

clue.text: Leaving booze wild duck swallows energy drink

definitions.note: a phrase describing someone, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside the body, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: the teal is a small wild duck
E is the symbol for energy
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A wild duck gulps an energy drink after giving up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' reads as one canned product, but it splits in two, and the duck does the swallowing. 'Wild' belongs to the duck, not the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teetotal abstains entirely from alcohol, which is what leaving booze alone amounts to.

clue.text: Centre for the audience does attract one

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is chosen for its sound

blocks.note: the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a central theatre attracts any audience at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb, but it is the plural of doe: female deer drawn to a male one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hart is an adult male red deer, the kind of stag that female deer are drawn to in the rut.

clue.text: Peril at pit that's collapsed — politician under scrutiny

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen apart, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A mine has fallen in, putting people in danger, and an MP now faces questions over it.
explanation.walkthrough: Priti Patel was a British Conservative cabinet minister, later Home Secretary, whose conduct drew repeated inquiries.
explanation.definitionFit: When the puzzle appeared she was a senior UK minister facing public criticism and investigation over her conduct.

clue.text: Ship rocks — vessel going round river

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: drinks served on the rocks come with ice
a beaker is a drinking or laboratory vessel
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A ship strikes rocks while another boat circles round on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'Ship' both suggest boats, but the vessel here is a beaker, and the rocks are the ice in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a ship with a strengthened hull built to clear a channel through frozen seas.

clue.text: Fate in Tyneside not completely appalling

indicators.note: not complete means the final part is missing, so the last letter goes
something appalling is a dreadful mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Life in north-east England is described as not quite dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in north-east England. Trim its last letter and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny and fate are synonyms for the predetermined course of events in a person's life.

clue.text: Green pipe going across road area

indicators.note: going across something spans it on both sides, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: a vent is a pipe or duct letting air or gas escape
Rd is the abbreviation for road
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A green-painted pipe has been laid across a stretch of road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road area' could be one thing, but it splits into two abbreviations that sit side by side inside the pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdant describes lush green vegetation, so it is a literary synonym for green.

clue.text: Songbird in roof — snug in the middle on top

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, so only those are kept
in a down entry, a piece placed on top comes first in the column

blocks.note: the two central letters of the word
thatch is a roof made of straw or reeds

explanation.surface: A little bird is tucked up snug inside a cottage roof, nesting high on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snug in the middle' reads as cosy at the centre, but it asks for the word's middle letters, placed above the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small European passerine bird with a whistling call, so it counts as a songbird.

clue.text: Temperature doubled in a drain almost causes crack

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature, written twice
to drain is to empty; cut short it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A doubling of temperature inside a drain makes it crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a fracture caused by heat, but it is the noun meaning a go, as in having a crack at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a crack at something is informal for making a try, so crack and attempt are synonyms.

clue.text: Supporter brings complaint about new player

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint
N is the abbreviation for new
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbles about the club's latest signing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' and 'player' suggest sport, but the player is an actor and the supporter a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help to a cause or person, so is a supporter in the patron sense.

clue.text: One avoiding Luke, at last in contact with his father?

indicators.note: at last points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept
touching means placed right beside, so the pieces are joined end to end

blocks.note: the final letter of the name
in Star Wars, Darth Vader is Luke Skywalker's father

explanation.surface: Luke Skywalker dodges his father before finally getting in touch with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Wars surface makes 'Luke' a character, but it only lends its last letter; 'his father' then names the famous villain.
explanation.definitionFit: An evader is a person who dodges or escapes something, so one avoiding is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Africans in university after simple accommodation

indicators.note: coming after means placed later, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: a hut is a basic, simple shelter
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Foreign students at a university settle for basic student housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In university' looks like a container instruction, but 'in' is a link and U simply follows the hut.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are the majority ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Circumnavigator on staff discovers magical plant

indicators.note: in an across entry, being on another piece means coming after it

blocks.note: to staff a post is to man it
Sir Francis Drake sailed round the world in the sixteenth century

explanation.surface: A round-the-world sailor among the crew finds an enchanted herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun for crew, but it is the verb to man.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake root, forked like a human figure, was credited in folklore with magical powers and a deadly scream.

clue.text: Topless brothel-keeper expelled gardener

indicators.note: without a top means the uppermost letter, the first in a down entry, is removed

blocks.note: a madam runs a brothel

explanation.surface: A topless bordello owner has been thrown out, along with the gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' seems part of the risque scene, but it is the instruction to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam tended the Garden of Eden in Genesis and was banished from it after the Fall, hence an expelled gardener.

clue.text: Declare invalid having to check blood type yearly

indicators.note: to check something is to stop it in its tracks, so one piece blocks the middle of another

blocks.note: to annul a marriage or contract is to declare it invalid
A is one of the ABO blood groups

explanation.surface: An invalid must have a blood test every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' tempts as a sick person needing a blood check, but 'Declare invalid' is the verb ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual means occurring once every year, a direct synonym of yearly.

clue.text: An heir dancing around gets rupture

indicators.note: dancing around means moving every which way, so these letters change places

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A young heir capers about too energetically and injures himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The dancing heir looks like the subject; the words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is an organ pushing through a weak spot in muscle, commonly called a rupture.

clue.text: About time to stop vice-president making false claim

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is lodged inside another

blocks.note: Mike Pence was US vice-president under Donald Trump
re means about or concerning
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is high time someone stopped a deputy leader telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time' reads as an exclamation of impatience, but it splits into RE and T, which go inside the vice-president's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a pretext or false show, a claim to something that is not true.
